items.name: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
items.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
items.description: Asynchronous monitoring, incident investigations, and compliance audits primarily rely on agent traces to reconstruct what happened. These analyses assume that LLM agents cannot tamper with their own execution traces. We show that local LLM agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Open Code and Grok Build fail to enforce this boundary. items.name: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
items.title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
items.description: Latent world models are typically trained to predict factual transitions, whereas model predictive control (MPC) must compare alternative actions from the same state. A model can therefore achieve low factual prediction error yet poorly distinguish candidate actions. We introduce AD-WM, an action-discriminative joint-embedding world model for counterfactual MPC. items.name: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
items.title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Distributed learning in embodied reinforcement-learning agents offers a degree of privacy by retaining raw sensor data on-device and transmitting only policy gradients to the server. items.name: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies
items.title: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies
items.description: Conspiratorial discourse on social media is not always expressed through explicit claims or stable lexical markers. The same surface content may express endorsement, legitimate concerns, criticism, satire, or mockery. The main challenge is therefore not only recognizing conspiracy-related claims, but inferring the speaker's intent -- the utterance's illocutionary force. items.name: RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations
items.title: RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations
items.description: Coding agents have demonstrated enormous success in solving complex programming problems. items.name: Rolling-WAM: World Action Models with Rolling Imagination
items.title: Rolling-WAM: World Action Models with Rolling Imagination
items.description: World Action Models (WAMs) couple action generation with future visual prediction for robotic manipulation. However, completing the joint video-action denoising process at each replanning cycle incurs substantial latency, delaying action updates and limiting closed-loop responsiveness. items.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models
items.description: Dedicated decision models such as Jev map unstructured language to probability distributions over finite choices, allowing their outputs to directly route requests, select tools, and trigger actions. Yet real-world inputs rarely arrive in isolation: they come with background details and surrounding context. items.name: SemMSA: Latent Semantic-Aided Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Data
items.title: SemMSA: Latent Semantic-Aided Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Data
items.description: Recent research on Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) has focused on learning from language, visual, and acoustic modalities with incomplete data to infer human sentiment. Most studies typically compensate for missing information by reconstructing modality features or designing complicated fusion mechanisms. items.name: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems
items.title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems
items.description: Task and motion planning (TAMP) problems remain difficult even with full observability and object-centric states because discrete decisions are tightly coupled to geometric, kinematic, and dynamic constraints. Generalized TAMP addresses this difficulty by exploiting regularities across problem instances to reduce planning effort on new instances. items.name: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
items.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
items.description: Online misinformation increasingly appears in spoken formats such as news clips, podcasts, interviews, political speeches, and social media videos, creating a need for fact-checking systems that can verify claims directly from speech. We introduce VeriSpeak, a probe benchmark for studying speech-based fact verification in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs). items.name: PoEM: Predicting RL Outcomes from Existing Policies
items.title: PoEM: Predicting RL Outcomes from Existing Policies
items.description: Foundation models are post-trained with reinforcement learning (RL) to maximize specific rewards, such as human alignment, correctness, or instruction following. This post-training process is computationally intensive, sometimes unstable, and has to be run from scratch every time the reward model changes or when we want to combine multiple rewards. items.name: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
items.title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
items.description: Existing point tracking models face a fundamental tradeoff: they can either track a sparse set of query points over long horizons, or track all points across only short clips. We introduce TrackEverything, a 3D point tracker that breaks this trade-off by representing videos as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates. items.title: Requirement-Bound Verified Commissioning: A Frozen Four-Billion-Parameter Local Model as a Candidate Generator under an External Acceptance Layer with Verification and Release Authority

items.name: Minimally Invasive Steering of Language Models
items.title: Minimally Invasive Steering of Language Models
items.description: Pre-logit steering adapts a frozen language model to a test-time reward by adding vectors to its final hidden states. Unregularized reward optimization can substantially alter the output distribution and degrade generation quality. items.name: Instrumental Monitor Evasion Emerges Under Ordinary Task Pressure
items.title: Instrumental Monitor Evasion Emerges Under Ordinary Task Pressure
items.description: A central concern in AI safety is that agents may treat oversight as an obstacle when it conflicts with completing their goals. We study instrumental evasion, the propensity of LLM agents to circumvent runtime monitoring as a means of completing ordinary tasks. items.name: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model
items.title: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model
items.description: We prove nearly quadratic lower bounds for randomized algorithms for linear optimization and uniform sampling over convex bodies in the membership oracle model. For linear optimization, this matches the known nearly quadratic upper bound up to a polylog factor in the dimension. For uniform sampling, this improves on the previous linear lower bound. Our construction also implies the same lower bound for volume estimation.

items.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems

items.title: The Alignment Illusion in Multimodal Large Language Models

items.name: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
items.title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
items.description: Large language model (LLM)-based clinical assistants are increasingly being integrated into electronic health record (EHR) systems, transforming how clinicians retrieve and synthesize information from patient records. items.title: ExplorationBench: Measuring AI Systems' Exploration in Verifiable Alien Worlds
items.description: Scientific discovery begins where known problems end. There, AI systems must engage in exploration: framing hypotheses, designing experiments, and iterating on the results. items.title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers
items.description: Latent neural surrogate solvers, or latent dynamics models, accelerate simulations of time-dependent physical systems by evolving a compressed latent space rather than resolving full-resolution fields directly. items.name: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance
items.title: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance
items.description: Long-horizon reasoning remains a central challenge for large language models (LLMs) under sparse-reward regimes. We argue that this brittleness arises from two biases induced by complex reasoning spaces: an exploration bias, where models are drawn toward locally plausible but structurally unstable branches, and a compounding bias, where small local deviations accumulate across depth and suppress rare rewards. items.title: Jev-Mobile: Jev as an Executor for Mobile GUI Agents
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a common foundation for autonomous mobile GUI agents, but most existing systems rely on the VLM for both planning and action grounding at nearly every interaction step, leading to substantial latency and model-serving cost. items.title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
items.description: U.S. employment-discrimination complaints describe complex event sequences that are not explicitly captured by lexical or embedding-based representations alone. items.description: We introduce GridSFM, a framework that combines a pretrained foundation model across grid topologies with physics-informed fine-tuning for solving AC Optimal Power Flow (AC-OPF) at scale. items.title: Do Audio Language Models Hear and Read Distinctive Features Alike?

items.title: A Training Criterion with Token-Level Tolerance to Transcription Ambiguity for Automatic Speech Recognition
